question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (a NORMAL Category III AIF, NOT a Large Value Fund) wants to run an Activist/Special-Situations play. What is the maximum percentage of Investable Funds (or NAV) it can commit to ONE investee company under SEBI AIF concentration limits?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 10.1.4.1, a regular Category III AIF cannot invest more than 10% of its Investable Funds or NAV in a single investee company. Large Value Funds enjoy a relaxed 20% cap. The Trap: Option C (20%) is the LVF relaxation — a real rule but only for LVFs. Option B (25%) is the Cat I/II close-ended concentration limit — WRONG category. Option A is a fabricated lower cap. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) tests 25% cap for Cat I/II close-ended. XIX-E: Cat III regular = 10%, Cat III LVF = 20%. Note the deliberate contrast. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 10% limit is tested on INVESTABLE FUNDS or NAV — whichever is LOWER at the time of investment. For open-ended Cat III, NAV drift can breach the limit passively; pre-set a 9% internal soft cap and a 10% hard stop in the OMS.
